The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

## claude.ai Windsor.ai
This MCP server provides access to the Windsor.ai API, which allows
retrieving analytical data from various data sources such as Facebook, Google Ads, and
more using connectors.

When interacting with this MCP server, follow these steps:

1. Call the "get_connectors" tool to get all available connectors and their connected
   accounts.
2. If a connector the user wants is not yet connected, call
   "get_connector_authorization_url" to get a link they can open in their browser to
   set it up (works for all connector types, OAuth and manual).

5. Call the "get_data" tool to retrieve data from a specific connector by providing

   and any options and filters if needed.

# Boldteq Website Analysis

## 1. Pages & Navigation Structure

**Primary Navigation:**
- Solutions (Web Development, UI/UX Design, Graphic Design, App Development - some marked "Coming Soon")
- How It Works
- Pricing
- Our Work
- Our Mission
- Resources (Blog, Help Center)
- Login / Schedule Demo

**Footer Links:**
- About, Services, Resources, Help sections
- Social media (LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook)
- Legal (Terms, Privacy Policy)
- Careers

## 2. Key UI Components

**Hero Section:** Tagline emphasizing "One Subscription. Predictable Execution" with CTAs for demo booking and 14-day trials

**Feature Highlights:**
- 14-day satisfaction guarantee
- No contract requirements
- Pause/cancel anytime flexibility

**Social Proof:** Featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Inc., Washington Post, Philadelphia, Technically

**Portfolio/Works Section:** Carousel showcasing Shopify, WordPress, Figma UI/UX designs, and banners

**Problem-Solution Framework:** Three agency pain points addressed (bottlenecked delivery, unreliable outsourcing, high hiring costs)

**Pricing Table:** Three-tier subscription model (Starter $999/month, Growth $1999/month, Pro $3499/month) with monthly/quarterly/annual billing options

**FAQ Section:** Eight expandable questions covering service details, pricing, and suitability

**Testimonials/Comparison:** "Traditional Way vs. Boldteq Way" showing delivery timeline improvements

## 3. Animations & Interactions

- Smooth scroll behavior across the page
- Gradient icon color transitions on navigation hover
- Carousel/slider functionality for portfolio items and client testimonials
- Typewriter effect cycling text ("Ownership Driven," "Without Hiring," "On Demand")
- Hover effects on feature cards with shadow/color changes
- Modal popup with fade-in animation for beta access offer
- Sticky navigation bar that appears after scroll threshold
- Slick carousel library for multi-slide galleries

## 4. Forms & Dynamic Elements

- Newsletter subscription form ("Join 500+ Subscribers")
- Chat widget (Chatwoot integration)
- Pricing plan selection buttons linking to checkout portal
- Demo booking CTA
- Beta access signup form
- Task submission interface mockup (shown in "How It Works")

## 5. Design Style

**Color Palette:**
- Primary: Dark navy (#092245, #082753)
- Accent: Cyan/turquoise gradients (#21cfff, #019ae6)
- Neutral: White, light grays
- Highlight: Yellow (#FFEB85)

**Typography:** Clean sans-serif, hierarchical heading structure

**Layout:** Grid-based responsive design with card components; asymmetrical sections alternating content/imagery

**Visual Elements:** Drop shadows, border-radius on cards, gradient overlays, icon illustrations

## 6. Integrations & Tracking

- **Google Analytics:** GTM setup (GA-VSPBSV4406)
- **Microsoft Clarity:** Web analytics tracker
- **Chatwoot:** Live chat/messaging widget for customer support
- **Webflow:** Website platform with built-in CMS
- **Slick Carousel:** JavaScript slider library
- **Trustpilot:** Review widget embedded (star ratings visible)

**Trust Signals:** Trustpilot reviews, media logos, founding date (2024), founder attribution (Yash)

Good, I have a clear picture of the current site. Here's my migration strategy:

## Webflow → Next.js Migration Strategy

### Two approaches to consider:

---

### Approach A: Clean Rebuild (Recommended)

**How it works:** Design and build each page/component from scratch in Next.js using your Stack A (Next.js 16 + Supabase + Railway), matching the current design pixel-for-pixel from screenshots/Figma.

**Pros:**
- Clean, maintainable code from day 1
- No Webflow bloat (Webflow exports messy HTML/CSS)
- Fully optimized for performance (Next.js SSG, image optimization, code splitting)
- Easy to extend with dynamic features (blog CMS via Supabase, dashboard, auth)
- Fits your existing Stack A perfectly

**Cons:**
- Takes longer than a direct export (~1-2 weeks for a site this size)

---

### Approach B: Export + Convert

**How it works:** Export Webflow HTML/CSS/JS, then convert each page into Next.js components.

**Pros:**
- Faster initial start

**Cons:**
- Webflow exports are bloated with unnecessary classes and inline styles
- You'll spend more time cleaning up than building fresh
- Animations (typewriter, carousels) need complete rewiring anyway
- Not recommended for production-grade output

---

### My Recommendation: Approach A (Clean Rebuild)

Your site has ~8-10 pages with well-defined sections. Here's what the build looks like:

| Page | Key Sections |
|------|-------------|
| Homepage | Hero (typewriter), social proof, portfolio carousel, problem/solution, pricing table, FAQ, testimonials, newsletter, CTA |
| How It Works | Step-by-step flow |
| Pricing | 3-tier table with billing toggle |
| Our Work | Portfolio gallery |
| Our Mission | About/story |
| Blog | CMS-driven (Supabase) |
| Login | Auth (Supabase) |
| Legal pages | Terms, Privacy |

**Tech decisions:**
- `framer-motion` for animations (typewriter, scroll reveals)
- `embla-carousel` for sliders (lightweight, accessible)
- Supabase for blog CMS + newsletter subscribers
- Chatwoot widget stays (simple script embed)
- PostHog replaces Google Analytics + Clarity
- Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui for all components

---

### What I need from you to start:

1. **Do you have the Figma designs for this site?** If yes, share the Figma link — I can pull exact specs. If no, I'll match from the live site screenshots.

2. **Do you want the blog to be CMS-driven via Supabase**, or static markdown files for now?

3. **Any pages or sections you want to add/remove/change** during the migration? (Good time to refresh anything outdated)

4. **Domain/DNS** — Are you managing DNS through Webflow or a separate registrar (Cloudflare, Namecheap, etc.)?

5. **Should I connect to your Webflow account** via the MCP integration to pull exact content/copy, or will you provide the copy separately?

Let me know these and I'll put together a detailed build plan.

**Next.js 16.2.3** — that's the current `latest` stable release, and it's exactly what your Stack A is locked to.

### Why 16.2.3 is the right pick:

- **Latest stable** — not canary, not beta, not RC
- **Next.js 16 is an LTS-grade major** — App Router is fully mature, React 19 stable, Turbopack is default
- **Long-term safe** — Next 15 is already in maintenance mode (backport channel at 15.5.15), Next 16 will be the primary supported version for the foreseeable future
- **Your other Boldteq projects already use it** — consistency across the factory

### What to avoid:
| Version | Why not |
|---------|---------|
| 15.x | Maintenance mode, won't get new features |
| 16.x canary/beta | Unstable, breaking changes possible |
| 14.x or older | Missing App Router improvements, React 19, Turbopack |

So the answer is straightforward: **Next.js 16.2.3 with React 19, TypeScript strict, Tailwind 4, pnpm**. That's your locked Stack A and it's the best choice right now.

content.thinking: The user is asking whether Tailwind 4 is better than Tailwind 3. Let me give a concise, practical comparison.

content.text:
Honest answer: **yes, but with a caveat.**

### Tailwind 4 wins:

- **No `tailwind.config.js`** — config lives in CSS with `@theme`, cleaner setup
- **Much faster** — new Oxide engine, noticeably quicker builds
- **CSS-first** — feels more natural, less JavaScript config
- **Smaller output** — better tree-shaking, lighter CSS bundles
- **Native CSS variables** — easier theming and dark mode

### The caveat:

- **shadcn/ui** — some components may still reference Tailwind 3 patterns. Most have been updated, but you might hit minor compatibility tweaks
- **Ecosystem** — a few third-party component libraries still target v3

### For the Boldteq website specifically:

It's a **marketing site** — no complex UI library dependencies. You're building components from scratch to match the Webflow design. Tailwind 4 is the clear pick here:

- Faster builds
- Cleaner config
- Future-proof (v3 will eventually go maintenance mode)
- No legacy constraints since it's a fresh project

### For Rankora:

I wouldn't migrate Rankora from v3 to v4 right now — it's working, and migration effort isn't worth it for a grandfathered project.

**Bottom line:** Tailwind 4 for all new projects, leave existing projects on v3. That's the right call.
why you not used tailwind 4 on that tgime ?

Good catch. You're right to call that out.

Rankora was built on **Stack A-Lovable** (Vite + React Router + Supabase) — it was a Lovable-generated project. Lovable's scaffold shipped with Tailwind 3 by default, and we kept it as-is since it was working.

It wasn't a deliberate choice to use v3 over v4 — it was just what Lovable gave us at the time.

Now that Lovable is archived and all new builds use **Stack A (Next.js 16 + Railway)**, Tailwind 4 is the default going forward. No repeat of that.

No real impact on Rankora. Tailwind 3 vs 4 doesn't affect:

- **Performance for users** — the CSS output is nearly identical in production
- **Features** — everything you can build in v4, you can build in v3
- **Security** — zero difference
- **SEO** — zero difference

The only things you're missing on v3:

| What | Impact |
|------|--------|
| Faster dev builds | Minor — you only notice on very large projects |
| Cleaner config | Developer convenience, not user-facing |
| CSS variables theming | Nice to have, but Rankora's theme is already set up |
| Future updates | v3 still gets patches, just no new features |

**Bottom line:** Rankora on Tailwind 3 is completely fine. No reason to touch it. Save migration effort for when there's an actual product reason — right now there isn't one.

For the Boldteq website, we start fresh with v4 and never look back.

content.text:
Here's the full stack breakdown for the Boldteq website:

### Core (Non-negotiable)

| Package | Why |
|---------|-----|
| **Next.js 16.2.3** | Framework — SSG for marketing pages, fast, SEO-optimized |
| **React 19** | UI library (comes with Next.js 16) |
| **TypeScript 5.8** | Type safety, strict mode |
| **Tailwind CSS 4** | Styling — utility-first, fast builds |
| **pnpm** | Package manager (not npm/yarn) |

### UI & Components

| Package | Why |
|---------|-----|
| **shadcn/ui** | Pre-built accessible components (buttons, cards, FAQ accordion, pricing table, dialogs) |
| **framer-motion** | Animations — typewriter effect, scroll reveals, hover transitions |
| **embla-carousel** | Portfolio slider & testimonials carousel (lightweight, 3kb) |
| **lucide-react** | Icons (already included with shadcn) |

### Content & SEO

| Package | Why |
|---------|-----|
| **next/image** | Built-in — auto image optimization, WebP, lazy loading |
| **next/font** | Built-in — self-hosted fonts, no layout shift |
| **@next/sitemap** or `next-sitemap` | Auto-generate sitemap.xml for SEO |

### Analytics & Monitoring

| Package | Why |
|---------|-----|
| **PostHog** | Replaces Google Analytics + Microsoft Clarity (one tool, privacy-friendly) |
| **Sentry** | Error tracking |

### Backend (only if you want dynamic features)

| Package | Why |
|---------|-----|
| **Supabase** | Newsletter subscribers, blog CMS, contact form submissions |
| **Resend** | Transactional emails (form confirmations) |
| **Zod** | Form validation |

### External (just script embeds, no install)

| Tool | How |
|------|-----|
| **Chatwoot** | Script tag in `layout.tsx` — same as current |
| **Trustpilot widget** | Script embed |

### Hosting

| Service | Why |
|---------|-----|
| **Railway** | Hosting (per Stack A) |
| **Supabase** | Database + auth + storage |

### What we're NOT installing:

- No Vercel, no Stripe, no Prisma, no NextAuth (per your Stack A rules)
- No Slick carousel (Webflow legacy — replaced by embla)
- No Google Analytics / Clarity (replaced by PostHog)
- No CSS modules (Tailwind only)

---

That's roughly **10-12 packages** total. Lean and intentional — nothing extra.

Want me to write up the full build plan now, or do you have questions about any of these choices?
